views.title: Outside: an upright box on a post
views.intro: A simplified drawing of Build 1. Every part is where it sits on the real node, and the mounting and the cable runs are drawn tidily.
views.alt: 3D drawing of the FALCON node: an upright grey box with the FALCON mark on its lid, fixed to a post, a black camera hood low on the lid and a rain plate on top of the hood.

callouts.name: Junction box
callouts.text: An ABS junction box, 195 × 115 × 75 mm, standing upright with its lid towards the bowl. It was sold as IP65. With holes drilled in it, it is no longer sealed to that standard.

callouts.name: Post mount
callouts.text: The box is fixed to a thin post, about 15 cm above the ground.

callouts.name: Rain plate
callouts.text: On top of the hood, leaning back against the lid, copper side up.

callouts.name: Camera hood
callouts.text: A black hood low on the lid keeps sun and rain off the camera.

callouts.name: One cable
callouts.text: A single Ethernet cable runs to the house. It carries power and data, so the yard needs no socket.

views.title: The camera head: lens, lights and weather sensor
views.intro: Looking up under the hood from the side of the bowl.
views.alt: 3D drawing looking up under the black hood: a camera lens with six infrared LEDs in a foam frame, a blue weather sensor below it and the copper rain plate above.

callouts.name: Rain plate
callouts.text: A bare copper comb. Water bridging its fingers reads as wet. It tells rain or dew from dry, not how much rain fell.

callouts.name: Hood
callouts.text: A black half-round hood on the lid.

callouts.name: Camera
callouts.text: A 1080p USB camera with a fixed-focus M12 lens, tilted slightly down.

callouts.name: Infrared LEDs
callouts.text: Six 850 nm LEDs light the scene at night. They reach about one metre, which is the limit of this rig's night vision.

callouts.name: Light sensor
callouts.text: Tells the camera when to switch between day and night. In the shade of the hood it sometimes gets this wrong.

callouts.name: Foam frame
callouts.text: Blocks of foam hold the camera board in place.

callouts.name: Weather sensor
callouts.text: A BME280 board for temperature, humidity and air pressure, set into the frame just below the camera, in the shade.

views.title: Underneath: every cable enters from below
views.intro: Looking up at the bottom of the box. Every opening is on the underside, where rain is least likely to get in.
views.alt: 3D drawing of the underside of the box: one large hole where all the cables enter and nine small holes for sound.

callouts.name: Cable hole
callouts.text: One hole of about 25 mm takes all four leads: Ethernet, camera USB, rain plate and weather sensor.

callouts.name: Leads from the camera head
callouts.text: The camera's USB cable, the weather sensor's lead and the rain plate's lead run down the lid and go in here.

callouts.name: Sound holes
callouts.text: Nine 2 mm holes let sound reach the microphones inside, and let some air through.

callouts.name: Ethernet to the house
callouts.text: Power over Ethernet from an injector indoors.

views.title: Inside: four things
views.intro: The box with its lid and camera head taken away. Only four parts live inside. Everything else is outside.
views.alt: 3D drawing of the open box: a Raspberry Pi under a blue audio board on the right, a black PoE splitter on the left and a small rain-sensor board at the top.

callouts.name: Rain-sensor board
callouts.text: The small comparator board that belongs to the rain plate outside. It turns the plate's resistance into a wet or dry signal for the Pi.

callouts.name: PoE splitter
callouts.text: Takes the power off the incoming Ethernet cable and feeds the Pi over USB-C. The data goes on to the Pi through a short network lead.

callouts.name: Audio HAT
callouts.text: A Waveshare DA7212 sound card stacked on the Pi, with two small microphones on the board. They hear the yard through the holes underneath.

callouts.name: Raspberry Pi 4
callouts.text: Mostly hidden under the audio board, mounted with its sockets pointing down. It captures and streams. It runs no AI.

callouts.name: Cable hole
callouts.text: All four leads come up through it.

callouts.name: Sound holes
callouts.text: The nine small holes, seen from inside.

views.title: In place: one metre from a water bowl
views.intro: The node watches one spot. The bowl is about half a metre across and about one metre away, which is as far as the infrared light reaches.
views.alt: 3D drawing of the node on its post facing a round water bowl about one metre away, with a dashed line from the camera to the bowl.

callouts.name: The node
callouts.text: On its post, with the bottom of the box about 15 cm above the ground.

callouts.name: Where the camera looks
callouts.text: The dashed line and the shaded fan are a sketch. They are not a measured field of view.

callouts.name: Water bowl
callouts.text: A shallow bowl with pebbles in it. Animals come back to water again and again, which is why the node watches it.

callouts.name: Cable to the house
callouts.text: Ethernet to the injector and the computer indoors.

hardware.what: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, 1 GB, Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit)
hardware.job: Captures video, sound and sensor readings and streams them. Runs no AI.

hardware.what: Arducam 1080p day and night USB camera: OV2710 sensor, fixed-focus M12 lens, six 850 nm infrared LEDs, automatic infrared filter
hardware.job: Watches the bowl at 1920 × 1080 and up to 15 frames a second.

hardware.what: Waveshare DA7212 Audio HAT (B), two microphones on the board, one channel used
hardware.job: Continuous sound at 48 kHz for bird calls, through small holes under the box.
Temperature, humidity and air pressure every 30 seconds.

hardware.what: Resistive rain plate with an LM393 comparator board
hardware.job: Wet or dry, read twice a second. After a wet reading the node keeps saying raining for 10 minutes.

hardware.what: PoE+ injector indoors (30 W), PoE splitter in the box
hardware.job: One Ethernet cable brings power and data.

hardware.what: ABS junction box, 195 × 115 × 75 mm, with a hand-made camera mount
hardware.job: Holds the Pi, the splitter and the rain board. This hand-made shell is the part to replace first.

hardware.what: Windows PC with an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti, FALCON running in WSL2 (Ubuntu)
hardware.job: Runs every model, stores the records and serves the dashboard.

roadmap.name: Build 1: the backyard prototype
roadmap.text: Camera, sound and weather on one node, visit rules, clips, a clean-up filter for night sound, weather history and a Camtrap DP export. The first release is tagged v1.0 in the repository.

roadmap.name: Recordings that cover the whole visit
roadmap.text: On 14 November a Bluethroat bathed at the bowl and the clip stopped after 10 seconds. Recordings are being changed to run for as long as the animal stays, with the sound on the same clip.

roadmap.name: A view-only page for friends
roadmap.text: Invited friends see the live picture, the visit log and clips, but no sound, no settings and no people. It is built and is being tested at home. How friends reach it from the internet is not decided yet.

roadmap.name: Build 2: one outdoor unit, one cable
roadmap.text: A weatherproof network camera with its own infrared replaces the webcam, for a sharper picture by day and a longer reach at night. The Pi keeps the microphones and the weather sensors. A TP-Link VIGI C340 is the current choice and has not been tested yet.

roadmap.name: Printed parts instead of hand-made ones
roadmap.text: A hood, a shaded holder for the weather sensor, a cradle for the rain plate and a post mount that other people can print and copy. This is what the 3D printer is for.

roadmap.name: A small computer instead of a desktop PC
roadmap.text: The same software on a Jetson-class computer, so that a home without a gaming PC can host a node. It has to match the PC's results on saved nights before it replaces it. This is what the mini PC is for.

roadmap.name: Plug in and use
roadmap.text: A pre-installed device: it starts its own hotspot, a phone joins it to the home Wi-Fi, and that is the whole setup. No cables to make, no command line.

roadmap.name: Export tried by a researcher
roadmap.text: The Camtrap DP export passes the standard's own checks. It has not yet been loaded into another person's tools. That test, with a researcher saying what is missing, comes before any claim that the data is ready for research.

roadmap.name: Pilots in other gardens
roadmap.text: Two friends' gardens first, each with the agreement of the people who live there, then a small pond. Solar power only where there is no mains.
